Chapter 8: Small Victories — Joy, Laughter, and the Light in Dark Times
You know, even in the middle of hardship and sorrow, there were these moments of pure joy that made everything else just... fade away.
Think about the birth of a healthy baby, or the sound of kids laughing as they play out in the street. Or maybe the quiet pride you see in a mother’s eyes after she’s made it through a tough labor.
Those are the moments that kept the midwives going.
Picture this: it’s a bright spring morning, and a midwife arrives at a home to find the whole family gathered in celebration.
There’s a brand new baby—pink and squalling—being passed around from hand to hand.
Every relative shares a blessing, or cracks a joke.
The mother, exhausted but absolutely glowing, is beaming with pride as her older kids dance and spin around the room.
For a little while, the midwife is swept up in the joy—her own worries just melt away.
And it wasn’t just these big celebrations. There were other victories—small but so important.
Like a mother who’d been sick finally regaining her strength and being able to look after her kids again.
Or a father, out of work for months, landing a new job and coming home with a fresh loaf of bread to share.
The midwives learned to spot those moments, to really savor them, and let them balance out the tough days.
And honestly, laughter became its own kind of medicine.
The midwives would swap jokes and stories with the families, finding humor in all the little absurd moments of daily life.
Even the nuns—who you might think were always serious—had their playful side.
Sometimes, they’d sneak extra biscuits to the midwives, or share funny stories from their own younger days.
What really stands out is that joy wasn’t just something that happened in spite of all the hardship.
So often, it happened because of it.
The families in the East End knew how to find those sparks of light, even in the darkest times.
And the midwives learned to do the same.
These moments of happiness—big or small—weren’t just a distraction.
They became a real source of strength, a reminder that life was always worth fighting for.
